messages:
infra-bot: ALERT: kv_cache_metadata_growth rate exceeded threshold on pv-cluster-7 (22:04 UTC). auto-scale attempted, failed 2/3. tagging incident S-2026-03-KV-META

maya: seeing a huge jump in metadata size across paged-kv pools, looks like continuous batching pushed many partial blocks into memory. currently +18GB in 6m.

sanjay: ETA on impact? are customers seeing errors or just latency?

maya: some tail latency spikes reported, a handful of internal test requests got 504s when blockmgr tried to load pages. customer-eng: one customer reported degraded LLM responses.

ellie: jumpstarted tracing for a sample request id=trace-8a9c. pulling logs from blockmgr on pv-cluster-7.

leo: I see repeated reallocation logs: `blockmgr: allocating block id=0x7ff.. size=20971520` then `blockmgr: metadata leak: refcount never released for block id`. pattern across hosts.

maya: hypothesis: a recent batching change increased max_continuous_batches and we ended up creating many short-lived KV block mappings; GC didn't release metadata fast enough.

ops-bot: INCIDENT BOT: Severity = P2. On-call paged: @sanjay. Please acknowledge.

sanjay: acknowledged. spinning up mitigation plan. Priority: avoid customer 5xxs.

maya: quick mitigation options: 1) rollback batch config to previous commit, 2) lower max_continuous_batches to 1, 3) force metadata GC across nodes (risky), 4) increase block eviction aggressiveness (short-term). I recommend 2 + 4 as fastest.

leo: prepared a hotpatch to set `max_continuous_batches=1` via runtime flag; can deploy to one region as canary in 90s. also a small change to eviction: `--block-evict-threshold=0.65` instead of 0.8.

ellie: I'll run the canary in us-west-2. readiness probe yes/no?

sanjay: go for canary. notify oncall and customers that we're performing live mitigation.

maya: customer-eng pinged the affected customer with a brief note. no SLA breach yet; they see increased latency but not full outage.

(30s later)

ops-bot: DEPLOY BOT: canary deploy started: runtime-evict-2026-03-01 to us-west-2-nodegroup-A.

leo: canary logs show metadata drop-off 6m after flag flip. memory pressure easing on those hosts.

ellie: latency tail reduced from 1.9s -> 0.8s for canary traces. no 504s in the last 3m.

sanjay: rolling to remaining nodes in us-west-2. keep other regions on watch.

maya: parallel task: investigating why GC didn't free metadata refs. looks like `batcher` holds transient handles until `on_flush` callback; recent refactor delayed the callback when batch assembled across shards. filing follow-up PR with corrected lifecycle.

leo: also patching blockmgr to log owner stack on refcount leak (non-prod first).

ops-bot: NOTE: scheduled temporary config change recorded under change-id CHG-1152. revert plan: auto-revert in 2h if no regressions.

(10m later)

ellie: us-west-2 rollout completed. us-east-1 and eu-west-1 still pending. us-east-1 showing similar metadata growth but slower.

sanjay: manual throttle applied to continuous batching at the LB layer for eu-west-1 to reduce burstiness while we deploy.

maya: customer-eng: the impacted customer reports improvement in LLM response consistency after canary. they downgraded severity to advisory.

customer-eng: thanks team. keep us posted on root cause and timeline for permanent fix.

(40m later)

maya: root cause summary so far: recent batching optimization (commit 5a3d1f) removed an early `flush()` in the cross-shard path. this allowed partial batches to accumulate metadata across shards until final assembly. combined with higher default `max_continuous_batches` we hit a pathological case where thousands of small partial mappings existed concurrently. GC didn't trigger fast enough because eviction thresholds were conservative.

sanjay: mitigation timeline: 1) immediate: lowered `max_continuous_batches` and tightened eviction thresholds (done). 2) short-term (24h): backport PR to reintroduce early flush in cross-shard path + extra safety refs. 3) medium (7d): add aggressive leak detection + automated metadata GC when growth-rate > X. 4) follow-up: add perf tests for partial-batch storm.

ellie: created incident ticket INC-2238 with timeline and playbook for oncall. tagging eng-runtime and eng-sre for postmortem.

leo: leave a note to avoid mem-opt changes to block size until after postmortem — we changed block size recently in a different release and want to separate variables.

ops-bot: INCIDENT BOT: Incident S-2026-03-KV-META updated to status: mitigated. please fill in postmortem template within 48h.

maya: thanks everyone. oncall handoff to @leo at 23:10 UTC. leo, please continue monitoring and run the GC audit script on the weekend.
